projects.projectName: Crane Clean Energy Center (TMI Unit 1 restart)
projects.notes: First-ever restart of a previously shut-down US commercial reactor. FERC approved transfer of 760 MW of Eddystone capacity interconnection rights (June 2026); NRC environmental assessment in final public comment (July 2026); fuel delivery on schedule for end of 2026. Restart targeted 2H 2027. DOE backed a $1B loan.

First plant authorized to return to operations after shutdown. Still offline as of Aug 2026: Holtec closed out the last major restart projects in July 2026 and moved to operational readiness, but has not announced a restart date.
Original BTM ISA rejected by FERC in Nov 2024. New framework moves 300 MW existing slice to front-of-meter; expansion staged to 1.92 GW by 2032.

projects.projectName: Clinton Clean Energy Center extension + uprate
projects.notes: Meta takes the entire 1.121 GW Clinton output. 30 MW uprate adds incremental capacity. PPA preserves the plant past its prior retirement date.
Option for a new 300 MW SMR at one of Vistra's existing nuclear sites.
AP1000 design under NRC review. Long lead time.

NRC renewed both units' licenses to 2044/2045 (April 2026), but California law still caps operation at 2030 and Gov. Newsom said in Aug 2026 he will not act to extend it this term. Underpins Silicon Valley datacenter load.
16 Aurora Powerhouse reactors x 75 MW each across a 206-acre site. Phase 1 delivers 150 MW. PJM interconnection applications filed (Q2 2026).
First corporate SMR PPA. Generation IV molten salt-cooled. Oak Ridge site.
24 x 77 MWe NuScale modules (1,848 MWe total) across Ohio and Pennsylvania sites with ENTRA1, announced Oct 2023. Little public progress reported since; not mentioned in NuScale's Q2 2026 results.
Largest single corporate renewable PPA disclosed. Multiple individual interconnection requests roll under this umbrella.

Alphabet closed its $4.75B acquisition of Intersect Power in March 2026. Construction began June 2026 on the 1 GW+ Meitner Energy Center in the Texas Panhandle (wind, solar, storage, gas firming co-located with a data center).
Wichita 805 MW + Mustang Creek 195 MW. Two 15-year PPAs announced Feb 2026 to serve Google's Texas data center operations.

4 of 8 buildings operational (~421 MW IT live) as of May 2026, missing the mid-2026 completion target; full buildout projected ~Nov 2026. The planned 600 MW expansion beyond 1.2 GW was scrapped in March 2026. 450,000 GB200s was the announced target, not current deployment. Powered by onsite gas + fuel cells.

4.5 GW additional Stargate capacity under the July 2025 Oracle agreement. US Stargate pipeline exceeded 9 GW across seven sites by April 2026 (Abilene, Shackelford Co TX, Dona Ana Co NM, Milam Co TX, Port Washington WI, Saline Township MI, Lordstown OH), six under construction. The Saline Township MI site (1.4 GW) is the load behind the DTE supply agreement tracked separately.
Meta formally expanded Hyperion to 5 GW in July 2026, lifting investment above $50B. Under construction since Dec 2024. Powered in part by the Entergy electric service agreement tracked separately.
First gigawatt-scale Meta supercluster at New Albany, publicly expected online in 2026. Booked at the announced ~1 GW; the earlier 1,020 MW / 500k-GPU figures were estimates without source support.

$10B+ campus, 13 buildings (10 data centers) delivering one gigawatt when fully operational; groundbreaking Feb 2026, ~4,000 peak construction jobs. The 1 GW is total campus capacity; Meta has not broken out critical IT load.

Capacity undisclosed: neither Meta nor developer Cambrin LLC has shared power draw, and no invented figure is carried. Pre-development agreement with the Town of Beloit (July 2025); DNR permitting activity Feb 2026; still not formally announced by Meta as of Aug 2026.

Facility 1 came online April 2026 (six weeks early); Microsoft declared it fully operational June 23, 2026, running OpenAI training on hundreds of thousands of GB200s. Microsoft discloses no MW (third-party estimates put facility 1 near ~300 MW critical IT; the prior 1,100 MW figure was unsupported). Program: a second $4B facility targets 2028, two further campuses approved Jan 2026, with Microsoft describing a path toward ~2 GW at Mt Pleasant.
Fifth building at the Midlothian campus: $880M, 288,000 sq ft per the TDLR filing; construction began Jan 2026. No public MW figure exists; the prior 400 MW was unsourced and is not carried.

AWS program in Caddo and Bossier Parishes (northwest Louisiana) plus a third Shreveport campus, developed by STACK Infrastructure with SWEPCO as utility; investment raised from $12B (Feb 2026) to $18B on Aug 18, 2026. Campus MW undisclosed; the prior 1,500 MW estimate is not carried. Distinct from Meta's Richland Parish Hyperion.

TVA-approved grid power now ~300 MW (original 150 MW plus a second 150 MW tranche approved early 2026). The 15-turbine permit (~247 MW, through Jan 2027) stands, but observed turbine counts have exceeded permitted levels and xAI faces Clean Air Act litigation over unpermitted operation.

Target 2 GW staged through 2027; first cluster (~110k GPU-class, ~210 MW IT) online early 2026. Onsite gas grew from 27 initial turbines to 46 operating (~495 MW) by May 2026, with 59 operating without federal permits per July 2026 records; a March 2026 Mississippi PSD permit authorizes a permanent 41-turbine (~1.2 GW) plant. NAACP Clean Air Act suit filed April 2026.

400 MW across three CoreWeave lease tranches (~$11B, 15-year terms). Building 1 (100 MW) in service ~Q4 2025; second building delivered July 1, 2026; third (150 MW) targets full capacity 2027. Campus engineered to scale to 1 GW.

300 MW critical IT on a 430 MW AI Factory campus for a US investment-grade hyperscaler (~$7.5B over ~15 years, April 2026); initial operations anticipated mid-2027. Applied Digital has not disclosed the state. A further 210 MW lease at Delta Forge 2 was announced June 8, 2026.

~833 MW of CoreWeave leases at Helios; a further 830 MW ERCOT approval (Jan 2026) doubled total approved+contracted capacity past 1.6 GW, with the new tranche positioned as multi-tenant runway rather than leased to CoreWeave. First CoreWeave phase delivering from early 2026.

1 GW West Texas site announced Nov 2025 as a JV (Cipher ~95% equity); fully executed 1 GW Direct Connect Agreement with AEP pending ERCOT approval. Development pipeline, not near-term load; no HPC lease announced yet. The prior 2026 date was wrong at entry.
Turnkey space + power for AI workloads.

$9.7B, 5-year Microsoft AI-cloud contract (GB300s, 20% prepayment): four 50 MW critical-IT Horizon data centers at the 750 MW Childress campus = 200 MW contract capacity (the prior 700 MW figure was an unsupported estimate). Horizon 1 delivered to and accepted by Microsoft Aug 13, 2026; Horizon 2-4 due later in 2026.

944 MW behind-the-meter combined-cycle gas + battery storage on ~1,400 acres in Greene County, PA, for an unnamed data center; deliberately behind-the-meter to bypass the PJM queue (turbine delivery 2028). Essential Utilities invested $26M for water and gas service.

Multi-GW co-located power+datacenter venture (Chevron, GE Vernova, Engine No. 1). First named offtake: Microsoft's 20-year Project Kilby PPA at Pecos, TX (June 2026), tracked separately; recategorized as a program aggregate to avoid double counting.

VoltaGrid is deploying up to 2.3 GW of modular gas generation (92 INNIO power packs at 25 MW, the largest order in INNIO's history, Oct 2025) across multiple Texas sites for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure AI data centers, with firm gas via Energy Transfer. Reclassified from anonymous generation to an Oracle offtake.
60 MW hybrid gas + battery system live and providing prime power at the Midwest hyperscaler site (Q2 2026); PROPWR total contracted capacity ~350 MW, contract carries expansion provisions.

projects.expectedOnline: Grid connection Dec 2026; full 1.4 GW within ~a year after
projects.offtaker: Stargate Saline Township campus (reported: Related Digital for Oracle/OpenAI)
projects.notes: DTE's first large data center supply agreement (Oct 2025, 1.4 GW, reported 19-year term). Michigan reporting and Epoch's site tracking identify the load as the Stargate campus in Saline Township, Washtenaw County. DTE cites ~3 GW more in late-stage negotiations plus 3-4 GW behind that. Counted as a supply deal on the same basis as the OpenAI-Georgia Power agreement; the load side is covered under Stargate additional sites.

~53.8 GW of data center capacity in stages of contracting as of Q2 2026 (up from 47.1 GW at the Q1 10-K), with ~12 GW under take-or-pay electric service agreements. Virginia DC requests ~70 GW total (last confirmed Q1 2026).

February 2026 update: $103B five-year capital plan (largest of any regulated US utility) with 14 GW of new generation plus 4.5 GW of battery storage; 4.5 GW of signed data center ESAs and ~9 GW pipeline.
Only new large US reactors completed in decades (~2,234 MW combined per Georgia Power; Unit 3 COD July 2023, Unit 4 April 2024). Underpins Southeast DC growth.

~$67B all-stock combination announced May 18, 2026 (0.8138 NEE per D share), billed as creating the world's largest regulated electric utility (~10M customers), explicitly motivated by data center demand. FERC and state applications filed July 15, 2026; Virginia SCC evidentiary hearings begin Nov 17, 2026; expected close 2H 2027.

811 projects totaling 220 GW submitted to Cycle 1 of PJM's reformed first-ready-first-served process (window closed April 2026): gas 105.8 / storage 66.5 / nuclear 17.9 / solar 14.8 / solar+storage 8.9 / wind 4.7 GW. After validation, 715 projects (201.5 GW) were accepted for study (Aug 2026); studies complete ~2028. The prior 258 GW figure contradicted PJM's own release.

~474 GW of large loads seeking interconnection as of June 2026, ~90% data centers (per ERCOT Senate testimony July 2026) — roughly double the late-2025 figure. ~205 GW eligible for the SB6 'Batch Zero' interconnection study beginning ~Sept 2026.
1,949 active generation interconnection requests totaling ~463 GW as of June 30, 2026: storage ~171 / solar ~162 / gas ~78 / wind ~48 GW.

910 active projects totaling 169 GW (MISO board update Dec 2025). Separately, 70 GW with signed interconnection agreements are not yet built (57% wind). MISO's expedited ERAS queue holds a further ~27 GW.

191.3 GW across 432 active projects at end-2025 (LBNL Queued Up 2026) — down sharply from 523 GW as Cluster 15 pause/resubmission withdrawals cleared; CAISO accepted no new requests in 2024-25, Cluster 16 opens 2026.
567.4 GW across 1,603 active projects at end-2025 (LBNL Queued Up 2026) — still the largest US queue volume, ahead of every ISO/RTO.
81% complete with 450+ MW delivering (Q2 2026); estimated cost rose ~$288M to ~$11.7B and full completion slipped ~6 months to end of 2027.

116 GW of gas turbine orders plus slot reservations at end of Q2 2026 (from 83 GW at end-2025 and 100 GW at Q1); 20 GW signed in Q2 alone, targeting 125+ GW under contract by end of 2026 with capacity ramping to 24 GW/yr by 2028. Most demand is data-center-driven gas.

Active gas capacity in US interconnection queues rose 86% in 2025 to 253 GW (LBNL Queued Up 2026); PJM's 2026 Cycle 1 intake was ~78% gas + storage by GW. Replaces an earlier 55%-of-new-entries stat whose FERC attribution could not be verified.

Alphabet raised 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195-205B in July 2026 (from $175-185B), the majority for servers, data centers, and networking. Replaces an entry that presented Google's 2019 $13B US announcement as 2026 data.
40 GW of renewable supply contracted since 2020 across 26 countries, 19 GW online, per Microsoft's Feb 2026 carbon-negative update. Largest corporate clean-power buyer.
Existing 300 MW co-location arrangement shifts to front-of-meter framework after PJM transmission upgrades.

FERC accepted PJM's Expedited Interconnection Track June 9, 2026; PJM began accepting applications July 31. Up to 10 requests per calendar year in 2026-27, >=250 MW unforced capacity, GIA within 10 months, online within 3 years; sunsets end of 2027. No awards yet.

Draft 16 TAC 25.194 (PUCT Project 58481, published March 2026) sets interconnection standards for loads >=75 MW: study fees $100k (75-249 MW) / $300k (250+ MW), $50k/MW financial security, site control requirements. Still proposed as of Aug 2026. ERCOT is implementing SB6 operationally regardless: Batch Zero (~205 GW) study begins ~Sept 2026.

FERC acted on its June 2026 deadline: Section 206 show-cause orders issued June 18, 2026 to all six RTOs/ISOs, directing them to justify existing tariffs or file reforms for large-load/data-center interconnection within 60 days, including expedited studies for co-located large loads. Earlier steps: PJM co-location transparency order (Dec 2025), SPP HILL process approved (Jan 2026).
Multi-site agreement to keep existing PJM nuclear plants serving Meta load. Plus the separate 300 MW SMR option.

projects.projectName: Oklo data center LOIs (two undisclosed operators)
projects.offtaker: Two undisclosed data center operators (LOIs, up to 750 MW)
projects.notes: Non-binding letters of intent announced Nov 2024 with two unnamed data center companies, up to 750 MW combined. Counterparties have never been disclosed.

Non-binding master power agreement to deploy up to 12 GW of Aurora powerhouses through 2044; individual binding PPAs expected as project milestones are reached. Took Oklo's order book from 2.1 GW to ~14 GW.
Two long-term PPAs announced May 2025 for 650 MW of solar in Texas and Kansas serving SPP, supporting Meta data centers.
Behind-the-meter gas plant co-located with a Microsoft-operated campus near Pecos. Majority GE Vernova turbines plus Solar Turbines units. Chevron FID expected end of 2026.

25-year electric supply agreement for OpenAI's self-built $20B+ Effingham County campus; up to 3.2 GW delivered in phases with up to 1,000 MW of demand response. OpenAI pays full infrastructure and service costs. Georgia Power plans new gas capacity partly to serve it.

projects.offtaker: Amazon Web Services (20-year PPA, up to 1,200 MW)
projects.notes: Existing Comanche Peak units; option to extend up to 20 more years. Supports Amazon's $5B data center project near the plant. Signed Sept 2025; Amazon confirmed as the customer in 2026.

projects.expectedOnline: Phases 1-2 under construction; full project by 2029
projects.notes: Largest planned US solar project: 2.5 GWdc solar + 2.9 GWh storage at full build in Wilson, AR. Google contracted the 1.6 GWdc first two phases; groundbreaking July 14, 2026. ~40 miles from Google's West Memphis data center.
200 MWac (250 MWdc) in LeFlore County with an 800 MWh BESS planned as phase 2; supports Google's Oklahoma data center operations. Enlight's first US commercial PPA.
490 MW solar + 235 MW/470 MWh battery in Matagorda County supporting Google's ERCOT data center operations.
RWE's first Oklahoma solar project, McCurtain County; power delivered into SPP for Google.
140 MWac (180 MWdc) in Freestone County; expands the Meta-Zelestra portfolio to ~1.4 GWdc across 8 US projects.
298 MWac in Bowie County, NE Texas; fourth RWE-Meta PPA since 2024 (portfolio now 872 MW). Construction began early 2026.
Two ERCOT projects totaling 220 MWac / 286 MWdc (Lucky 7 100 MWac, Pepper 120 MWac); Meta takes 100% of output and environmental attributes.
150 MWac (172 MWdc), $237M project in Acadia Parish; supports Meta's Louisiana energy expansion.
100 MWac (140 MWdc), $300M project in Klickitat County; fourth US Avangrid-Microsoft project, joint contracted capacity now over 500 MW.
~750 MW of behind-the-meter medium-speed gas engine capacity for Crusoe's US AI data center fleet: 438 MW firm contract plus a 310 MW letter of intent. Sites not disclosed.
~$3.2B combined-cycle plant, 15-year minimum term with extension options and potential expansion to 2.4 GW. Principal commercial terms agreed (Aug 2026); not yet a signed definitive agreement.

projects.offtaker: Oracle (MSA up to 2.8 GW; 1.2 GW initial)
projects.notes: Master agreement (April 2026) for up to 2.8 GW of gas-fed solid-oxide fuel cells across Oracle projects; 1.2 GW initially contracted (booked here). Project Jupiter (Dona Ana County, NM, up to 2.45 GW) is the first major site; its gas pipeline slipped to Feb 2027. Missed by the prior refresh.

projects.projectName: Savannah River Site AI energy project (Amentum)
projects.notes: NNSA selected Amentum (July 2026) to negotiate a phased lease for a 1 GW AI data center backed by ~2 GW of on-site generation, gas first with a planned transition to advanced nuclear. Selection only; not a final lease or PPA.

~2.5 GW across 13 signed agreements (Dec 2025): up to 2.1 GW solar from nine projects in ERCOT/SPP/MISO plus 190 MW solar + 168 MW battery storage in New Mexico. Builds on ~500 MW of operating NextEra projects Meta already contracts.

1.17 GW of wind and solar across Missouri, Texas, and West Virginia serving Google data centers in SPP, ERCOT, and PJM; over $2.4B investment. Brings the partnership to 1.24 GW with an existing WV PPA.

Seaway Wind TX 196 MW, Yellow Wood Solar OH 300 MW, Pleasant Prairie Solar OH 140 MW, Decoy Solar AR 155 MW; energy to local grids with Meta taking the clean-energy credits. Invenergy puts the full Meta partnership at 1,800 MW including earlier tranches.

20-year, 100 MW PPA with NV Energy through 2050 over a portfolio of Zanskar-built geothermal projects serving Amazon's Reno-area data centers; Amazon covers all costs. Contingent on PUCN approval of NV Energy's 2026 IRP. Amazon's first data center geothermal.
600 MW solar plus 600 MW battery storage announced alongside the Zanskar geothermal PPA for the same Reno-area data center load; Amazon covers costs so they are not passed to Nevada ratepayers.

150 MW closed-loop, water-independent geothermal delivered to the PNM grid for Meta's New Mexico data center operations; ~$1B investment. Exact PPA terms undisclosed, so booked as a signed partnership rather than a firm PPA.

projects.expectedOnline: Power by end of 2029; capture early 2030
projects.offtaker: Google (offtake for most of the plant's output)
projects.notes: First corporate offtake agreement for a CCS-equipped gas plant: 400+ MW at ADM's Decatur complex with ~90% of CO2 stored in ADM's Class VI wells. Google's exact contracted share undisclosed; 400 MW is plant capacity.

Amazon bought the shovel-ready 1.2 GW Sunstone solar + co-located storage project in Morrow County from bankrupt Pine Gate Renewables for $83M; court-approved Jan 2026. An asset acquisition rather than a PPA.

LPSC approved 4-1 on Aug 20, 2025: three new CCGTs for the Hyperion campus (Franklin Farms 1 and 2 ~778 MW each, Waterford 5 820 MW, ~$3.2B). ESA runs Dec 2026-Nov 2041 with 5-year auto-renewals; Meta pays via a single-customer tariff sized to recover the full revenue requirement. A seven-plant expansion (to ~7.5 GW total gas) is pending LPSC approval and is not booked here.

First direct corporate PPA for fusion power: 200 MW from CFS's first commercial ARC plant in Chesterfield County, roughly half its planned output; announced June 30, 2025 alongside a Google equity investment. Pre-construction and technology-contingent.
